chapter: Early influences, Oliver date and trombone peers
title: Jack Teagarden after-hours
summary: He recalls keeping Teagarden playing Tiger Rag in every key until morning and drinking with him.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: What is your impression of Jack Teagarden? (no answer)
How many times did you two work together? Just on occasion?

No, see when I first came to New York ( ? ) so, anyway ... I'm not afraid to play with nobody... we'd get to work in the morning and every morning here's Jack Teagarden about 4 o'clock after the place had closed, I caught him. O'Neil Old Dale Spencer came and got me out of bed ... ( ? ) Willie the Lion Smith nothing but the piano ... and he was playing in the Nest ( ? )

... like this and I kept him there until 8 o'clock in the morning. I said, 'You ain't going nowhere.' Played Tiger Rag in every key. Every time he'd start off, I said, 'No, you're not.' Then, you know, sometimes they have agents and that things and you don't know who's listening to you. So, he decided to get up a cavalcade for jazz and Jack, he got _______.
So, we played and we got; Jack could play, too. And, he's a helluva executioner but I never ... I never called that jazz music
Every night he came to work, he drank and I drank. He had a special quart in a case, playing my horn. ... we were friends, we just played ... liked to have fun.
